pull.title: Configuration argument handling improvements.
pull.body:
Several numeric options were read with GetArg<int>() and then stored into unsigned or wider members without a range check. A negative value wrapped to a huge value and disabled the limit it was meant to configure, and a value wider than the destination could silently become a different number.

Parse the options whose destination is unsigned with ToIntegral<T>() on the raw string rather than with GetArg<T>(): the typed getter saturates values it cannot represent (so a leading '-' for an unsigned T becomes 0), while ToIntegral rejects '-', trailing garbage and overflow instead of saturating. Reject the remaining out-of-range values where they are read:

- -maxtipage: uint32_t seconds, range [0, UINT32_MAX]. A negative age placed the IBD cutoff in the future, so the node never treated its tip as recent.
- -dbbatchsize: uint64_t bytes. A negative value wrapped to a huge batch size and disabled flushing, so a reindex could hold an unbounded batch.
- -dbcrashratio: uint32_t, range [0, UINT32_MAX]. CoinsViewOptions::simulate_crash_ratio is changed from int to uint32_t to match.
- -limitclustercount: [1, MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT_LIMIT]. The separate upper-bound check in ApplyArgsManOptions is folded into this one, so an invalid value is reported once with one message.
- -limitclustersize: [1, INT64_MAX / 1000] kB. Zero made every transaction exceed the cluster size and blocked all mempool admission.
- -limitancestorcount, -limitdescendantcount: non-negative.
- -mempoolexpiry: [0, std::chrono::seconds::max() / 3600] hours, and the value is stored as seconds directly. The bound is taken from seconds rather than hours because std::chrono::hours is not guaranteed to be 64-bit.
- -datacarriersize: [0, UINT_MAX]; still unchecked when -datacarrier=0 turns the limit off.
- -bytespersigop: [0, UINT_MAX]. A negative value wrapped and inflated the sigop-adjusted size of every transaction until all were non-standard.
- -maxsendbuffer, -maxreceivebuffer: [0, UINT_MAX / 1000], since both are multiplied by 1000 into unsigned int members.
- -bantime: greater than 0. Zero or negative made setban without an explicit duration create an already expired ban.
- -timeout: positive and at most INT_MAX milliseconds. A non-positive value now fails instead of silently falling back to the default (as -peertimeout already did), and a value above INT_MAX used to narrow before it could be checked (e.g. 2^32 + 1 became 1).
- -txconfirmtarget: [1, UINT_MAX] in parameter interaction, and additionally bounded by the fee estimator's maximum when a wallet is loaded. A target beyond the estimator's range made every transaction fall back to -fallbackfee. The help text now states the minimum.

Zero remains valid wherever it already meant "disabled": -dbbatchsize, -datacarriersize, -mempoolexpiry, -maxtipage, -bytespersigop, -maxsendbuffer, -maxreceivebuffer, -limitancestorcount and -limitdescendantcount.

Since -nofoo is parsed as 0, add DISALLOW_NEGATION to the options where 0 is valid but very different from "no limit": -dbbatchsize, -mempoolexpiry, -maxreceivebuffer, -maxsendbuffer, -maxtipage, -limitancestorcount, -limitdescendantcount and -datacarriersize. Options that already reject (-bantime, -timeout, -peertimeout, -limitclustercount, -limitclustersize, -txconfirmtarget) need no separate check: negation reports the value error once. -bytespersigop still allows negation, because 0 turns the sigop adjustment off, which is exactly what -nobytespersigop says.

ReadCoinsViewArgs now returns util::Result<void> (marked [[nodiscard]]) so its errors abort startup instead of being discarded.

Finally, -help gains the =<n> placeholder for the options that take a value (-dbbatchsize, -bytespersigop, -datacarriersize, -stopatheight, -checkblockindex) and states the bounds for -bantime, -limitclustercount, -limitclustersize and -txconfirmtarget.

Add unit tests for the option parsers and functional tests for the accepted, rejected and negated forms.

Concept ACK

There are lots of AI findings about these potential misconfigurations, so it would be good to close off as many of them as possible in one go.

A few closely related cases seem worth covering as well:
- `-timeout` values above `INT_MAX` are narrowed before the new positivity check (similar ones were already attempted here and closed).
- Very large `-mempoolexpiry` values can overflow when converted from hours to seconds.
- A negative `-txconfirmtarget` wraps into the wallet's unsigned target and can make fee estimation fall back to `-fallbackfee`.
- Negating an integer option is documented as setting it to `0`, so `-nolimitclustersize` and `-nobantime` are equivalent to the zero values this PR explicitly accepts. `-limitclustersize=0` makes every transaction oversized and prevents normal mempool admission, while `-bantime=0` makes `setban` without an explicit duration create an immediately expired ban.

CI seems to fail because the new test loop binds a `std::string` reference to temporary strings.

See https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36763

But I think I'm Approach NACK at yet another piecemeal approach to a solution for this. This should be solved by the args handler itself, not with many different bug prone special cases.

Concept ACK 1ab3f148582c21054dfc9323623edcf9768949f6 for parsing improvements here, but I'd recommend against increased use of the DISALLOW_NEGATION flag:

- If your option can't accept zero values, DISALLOW_NEGATION is only a partial fix and may allow zeroes to slip through because you are only guarding against them being set ib a single path. Better to check for valid values one place instead of multiple.
- It creates inconsistent UX where -option=0 and -nooption have different behaviors without a clear reason, when normal behavior is for them to behave the same.

DISALLOW_NEGATION was intended to used rarely and eventually removed (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/22766#issuecomment-944924866) and this PR seems to increase usage by a lot. The other changes here look very good though.

---

**Edit:** My comment above about `DISALLOW_NEGATION` was overbroad. The flag does make sense for limit options where "no limit" and 0 mean different things, see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36861#pullrequestreview-5943499719.

Concept ACK

There is a bit of overlap between this and https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36880 and I didn't catch the overlap because I looked for related PRs before this PR here was opened. This particularly focusses on the "-no..." flags behavior. It may be a little bit better in some parts but others may still be considered too "piecemeal".

I could drop parts of my PR to remove the overlap but I would first like to see if the approach should be completely different. I am particularly interested in fixing the `-no...` options that either do the complete opposite of what's expected or even prevent startup or can crash the node. I think that is worth fixing even with a more priecemeal approach but I am also fine if these can drive a faster implementation of fixes within argsman.

re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36861#pullrequestreview-5899222221

Correction to my earlier review: I overstated the case against `DISALLOW_NEGATION`, sorry about that. It makes sense for options that are a maximum, limit, or timeout, where `-nofoo` reads as "no limit" but 0 means something very different. Ideally `-nofoo` might mean unlimited for these, but since negation has always meant 0, an error is the safest choice.

I still think negation should generally behave like setting 0 or empty values, and if these values are invalid, better to check for them once than have multiple checks producing different errors. By that standard, about half of the uses here look right to me, and the rest aren't needed:

- Make sense: `-dbbatchsize`, `-mempoolexpiry`, `-maxreceivebuffer`, `-maxsendbuffer`, `-maxtipage`, `-limitancestorcount`, `-limitdescendantcount`, `-datacarriersize`.
- Not needed because the PR already rejects 0, so `-nofoo` would get that error: `-bantime`, `-timeout`, `-peertimeout`, `-limitclustercount`, `-limitclustersize`, `-txconfirmtarget`.
- Not needed because 0 means what `-nofoo` says: `-bytespersigop`, where 0 turns off the sigop adjustment.

Updated negation support:

-bantime → Error: -bantime must be greater than 0 (got 0).
-timeout → Error: timeout must be a positive integer.
-peertimeout → Error: peertimeout must be a positive integer.
-limitclustercount → Error: limitclustercount must be between 1 and 64 (got 0)
-limitclustersize → Error: limitclustersize must be between 1 and 9223372036854775 kilobytes (got 0)
-txconfirmtarget → Error: -txconfirmtarget must be between 1 and 4294967295 (got 0).
-bytespersigop → accepts negation silently, since 0 means "no sigop adjustment"

Each is now validated in exactly one place, and -nofoo produces the identical message to -foo=0

Code review ACK 9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd. This makes numeric options that master silently accepts with nonsensical values (negative buffer sizes, ban times and confirmation targets, `-timeout=0`), or that crash the node (`-limitclustercount=0`), fail at startup with clear errors instead. I tried each changed option on regtest with valid, out-of-range and negated values, and they all behaved as described.

I still think these checks would be better in ArgsManager (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36861#discussion_r4682944029), but the changes are an end-user improvement either way and I didn't see other significant problems.

comments.body: this fix seems wrong. The correct fix would be to just parse as u32. Note that chrono itself can't deal with i64 here: `std::chrono::seconds 	std::chrono::duration</* int35 */>`
parsing should be done as u32?

I know that parsing saturates, but I am not sure if it is the right fix to do manual parsing one-by-one at each call site.

This is adding tens of lines of code for what is basically a debug-only option. Also, it takes away the saturation "feature" here.


I think we'll have to decide:

* Either we keep the saturation feature, and just use dumb parsing, or
* we do proper validation, but then inside the argparser, to avoid re-inventing the wheel for every call site.

Maybe this can be done with a new Getter that takes an options object with the upper and lower bound and then it returns either nothing (if nothing was set), or the value (if it fits the range), or the error (if it doesn't fit the range, or so)?

re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36861#discussion_r4614637883

In commit "Configuration argument handling improvements." (9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd)

> we do proper validation, but then inside the argparser, to avoid re-inventing the wheel for every call site.

+1 for doing the validation in ArgsManager. Besides the extra code, doing it at each call site means options in this PR now parse numbers differently. For example, `-limitclustercount=2.5` is an error, but `-limitclustersize=2.5` is silently treated as 2, because `GetIntArg` [ignores](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd/src/util/strencodings.h#L130) anything after the leading digits, while the [`ToIntegral`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd/src/util/strencodings.h#L184-L186) call used for `-limitclustercount` rejects it. The error messages also vary ("-bantime must be...", "limitclustersize must be...", "timeout must be a positive integer.").

A getter like you describe could be something like:

```cpp
//! Return nullopt if the option is not set, the value if it is an integer in
//! [min, max], or an error if it is not an integer or is out of range.
template <std::integral Int>
util::Result<std::optional<Int>> GetArg(const std::string& name, Int min, Int max) const;
```

That would make each call site one line and give every option the same parsing and error format. It would also fit #31260, which turns `GetArg` default arguments into compile-time setting declarations and could handle min and max arguments the same way.

re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36861#issuecomment-6979485030

In commit "Configuration argument handling improvements." (9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd)

> Each is now validated in exactly one place, and -nofoo produces the identical message to -foo=0

Thanks, this looks right to me now. `DISALLOW_NEGATION` is used only for the limits where "no limit" and 0 mean different things, and the other options give the same error for `-nofoo` and `-foo=0`.

In commit "Configuration argument handling improvements." (9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd)

The commit message and PR description still say `-limitclustersize=0` and `-bantime=0` remain valid, but this code now rejects 0 for both ([`-bantime`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd/src/init.cpp#L1214-L1216) too), so they could move to the list with `-limitclustercount` and `-timeout`.

The same paragraph says 0 still means "disabled", but for several of these options 0 is the strictest setting rather than disabled: `-maxsendbuffer=0` pauses sending whenever anything is queued, `-maxtipage=0` keeps the node in IBD, and `-mempoolexpiry=0` expires every transaction. It could just say that these options still accept 0. The [Ralph review](https://review.fish.foo/report/36861-aa8bfe2a137cceda68737c2874c5367f655dc5db-2656-1.html#finding-finding%3A6) pointed this out too.

In commit "Configuration argument handling improvements." (9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd)

I think this comment has the effect backwards. [`Expire()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd/src/txmempool.cpp#L865) removes entries older than the cutoff, so a cutoff in the future would expire every transaction at the next check, not stop them from expiring. Maybe: "so a negative value would move the expiration cutoff into the future and expire every transaction." The [Ralph review](https://review.fish.foo/report/36861-9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd-2794-6.html#finding-finding%3A6) caught this.

In commit "Configuration argument handling improvements." (9611ea5584050b6decbeec528d5dfafabee6adbd)

Could this add a release note? Some configurations that start on master will fail to start after this change, for example `-timeout=0` (which currently falls back to the default), `-bantime=0`, `-limitclustersize=0`, and `-txconfirmtarget=0` or above 1008 when a wallet is loaded. A short note listing the options that now reject out-of-range values would help anyone who hits one of the new errors after upgrading. The [Ralph review](https://review.fish.foo/report/36861-aa8bfe2a137cceda68737c2874c5367f655dc5db-2656-1.html#finding-finding%3A5) suggested this too.
